players.note: TJ Hockenson will play this week (wrist). He had limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday, but he had a full session on Friday. Hockenson doesn't carry an injury designation into this game. Hockenson is TE9 in fantasy points per game with a 19.1% target share, 2.01 YPRR, seven red zone targets, one deep target, and a 20.3% first-read share. Hockson should be a TE1 again this week. Over their last five games, the 49ers have allowed the tenth-most yards per target, the fifth-most receiving fantasy points per game, and the fifth-most fantasy points per game to tight ends.

I don't trust Daniel Jones at all. The only Colts' pass catcher I'll remotely consider for a fantasy lineup until further notice is Tyler Warren. Last week, with the Colts' passing-catching room decimated, Warren only had a 13.6% target share, two receptions, one receiving yard, and a 7.1% first-read share. Someone on the Indy coaching staff needs to explain that to me like I'm five years old because I don't get it. Overall, Warren is the TE7 in fantasy points per game with a 21.4% target share, 1.18 YPRR, five red zone targets, and a 20.4% first-read share. I don't expect Warren to have a wonderful game in Week 11. Over their last five games, Houston has allowed the 12th-fewest yards per target and the seventh-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Since Week 7, Chig Okonkwo has had a 71.9% route share, a 19.6% target share, 1.38 YPRR, one red zone target, one deep target, and a 22.2% first-read share. Okonkwo is on the streaming radar this week. Over their last five games, Cincy has ranked 15th in receiving fantasy points per game allowed to tight ends and 19th in fantasy points per opportunity.

Brenton Strange is quietly having a strong season, but the Jags blowing other teams out has hurt him. Strange is TE9 in XFP per route, but he is also 23rd in routes run. Strange has a 15.3% target share with 1.90 YPRR, four red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 16.6% first-read share. Sit Strange this week. Over their last five games, New York has held tight ends to the seventh-fewest yards per target and the tenth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Well, it was nice to learn last week that Mark Andrews has been playing through a broken hand. It would have been nice to know that weeks ago. (And people wonder why I wear a tin foil hat with injury reporting). Andrews is reportedly back to full health, and he looked the part last week with a 16.3% target share, a 60.8% route share, 2.65 YPRR (82 receiving yards), one red zone target, and a 16% first-read share. His resurgence will be put to the test this week. Over their last five games, Carolina has held tight ends to the tenth-fewest yards per target and the 13th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

After two strong games of snap usage and route share, Mike Gesicki saw his role crater last week with a 40% snap rate and a 45.7% route share. Gesicki had only a 4.5% target share. It's just a horrible reminder that his role is quite volatile. Overall, he has a 54.5% route share, an 8.2% target share, 1.30 YPRR, six scores, six red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 10% first-read share. Gesicki is on the streaming radar again this week, though. The matchup with Washington is nice. Over their last five games, they have allowed the 11th-most yards per target and the second-most receiving fantasy points per game to tight ends.

Dallas Goedert is the TE11 in fantasy points per game. In his last game, with Joe Milton under center, Goedert had a 75% route share, a 17.6% target share, 1.39 YPRR (50 receiving yards), one deep target, and a 9.5% first-read share. Overall, he has a 16% target share with 1.72 YPRR, three red zone targets, and an 18.6% first-read share. Goedert could be a TE1 again this week. Over their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the sixth-most yards per target and the 13th-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Dalton Schultz's role in the Houston passing attack has withered. Over his last two games, he has had only a 55% snap rate, a 58.5% route share, a 6.7% target share, 1.10 YPRR (53 receiving yards), and a 4.2% first-read share. Schultz is the ultimate desperation, deep league streaming option this week, and it's only because of the matchup. Across their last five games, Indy has allowed the second-most yards per target and the most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Darren Waller has two TE1 outings this season in weekly scoring (TE5, TE1). Since Week 8, he has had a 57.4% snap rate, a 64.5% route share, a 13.6% target share, 1.56 YPRR, two red zone targets, and a 16.9% first-read share. Waller is a borderline TE1/strong streaming option this week. Over their last five games, Baltimore has allowed the fifth-most yards per target, the tenth-most receiving fantasy points per game, and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends. Waller has been listed as questionable (knee). He had limited practices on Thursday and Friday and is expected to play.

Last week, with Fernando Mendoza under center, Michael Mayer had a 10.3% target share, 16 receiving yards (0.52 YPRR), and a 10% first-read share. Overall, he has a 13.6% target share with 1.54 YPRR, three red zone targets, one deep target, and an 11.6% first-read share. Mayer has two TE1 finishes in weekly scoring this season (TE7, TE6). Mayer is on the streaming radar this week. Across their last five games, Denver has allowed the most receiving fantasy points per game and the seventh-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Cade Otton is a deep-league streaming option only. In Jalon Daniels' three starts, Otton had a 10.5% target share with 0.72 YPRR, zero red zone targets, zero deep targets, and an 11.6% first-read share. The most appealing thing about Otton this week is the matchup. Over their last five games, Detroit has allowed the 12th-most yards per target and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends. *UPDATE:Â Let's also discuss Otton's production and such with Baker Mayfield under center in case he does play this week. In Otton's six games played with Baker Mayfield, he has had a 17.9% target share with 1.06 YPRR, six red zone targets, and a 21.4% first-read share. Otton would get a definite bump in usage from those numbers with Mayfield under center, but my counterargument would be that, considering the matchup this week, Otton should already be a solid part of the Bucs' game plan. He'd still just be a streaming option at the tight end position with maybe a tad more shimmer.

Juwan Johnson's role in the New Orleans passing attack has shriveled to nothing. Since Week 6, he has had only a 58.5% snap rate, a 61.5% route share, a 5.8% target share, 0.70 YPRR, and a 9.2% first-read share. He has a glorious matchup this week, but I don't know if he'll see enough volume to take advantage of it. Over their last five games, Chicago has allowed the seventh-most receiving fantasy points per game and the eighth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends. With the role reduction, Johnson is only a deep league streaming option this week.

With Dalton Kincaid doubtful this week (thumb/ankle), Dawson Knox is a viable streaming option at tight end this week. Knox has a 14% TPRR with 0.65 YPRR, four red zone targets, one deep target, and 0.038 first downs per route. With Knox's run-blocking abilities, I expect Knox to have a stronger snap rate and route share this week than we've seen from Dalton Kincaid this season. Miami continues to struggle to defend tight ends. Over their last five games, Miami has allowed the 12th-most receiving fantasy points per game and the tenth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Darnell Washington remains on the streaming radar this week. The low end of it, but he is on it. Since Week 5, Philly has had the tenth-highest single-high rate (57.9%). Against single-high, Washington has a 24% TPRR and 2.48 YPRR. Last week, he had a 51.7% snap rate, a 36.1% route share, a 9.4% target share, and a 10% first-read share. Over their last five games, Philly has ranked 18th in yards per target and given up the 12th-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Mason Taylor is on the streaming radar this week. Since Week 6, he has had a 64.1% snap rate, a 54.5% route share, a 13.9% target share, 1.42 YPRR, five red zone targets, and a 14.2% first-read share. The Bolts have been a favorable matchup for tight ends this season. Over their last five games, the Chargers have allowed the most yards per target and the sixth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends. Taylor could flirt with TE1 production this week. Taylor has one TE1 outing this season (TE2 in Week 7).

Well, Dalton Kincaid's role in the Buffalo passing attack sucks again. Since Week 8, he hasn't had more than a 56.6% snap rate or a 56.8% route share in any game. Since Week 8, Kincaid has had a 51.6% route share, a 51.7% snap rate, a 14% target share, 3.51 YPRR, two red zone targets, three deep targets, and an 18.3% first-read share. He's essentially returned to his 2025 role, which is so depressing. It limits his weekly ceiling and drops his floor. Kincaid could be a TE1 again this week, though. Miami continues to struggle to defend tight ends. Over their last five games, Miami has allowed the 12th-most receiving fantasy points per game and the tenth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.
